sources.citation: Natterer, Johann. 1817-1835 [Cabixi list 1828-29]. Wortlisten von Indianersprachen in Brasilien. Universitätsbibliothek Basel, Nachlass Tschudi, UBH T 2; section 'Sprache der Indianer Cabexis', scan labels [407]-[414]. doi:10.7891/e-manuscripta-128842.
sources.note: PRIMARY SOURCE (8 ms. page scan saved). Header: 'Proben der Indier Cabixis – von einem Jungen der klein nach Mattogrosso gebracht wurde – er heißt Schirinimõ. – Seine Nazion nennt er Piacá.' Wordlist in Kurrent with macrons, graves, acutes and underlining on forms (Uvà, Tschitschānā, Hānné, Na̲ka̲ri̲); no key to the diacritics and no remark on accent.
'It may have been tonal', citing Adelaar & Brijnen 2014 (third-hand); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Campbell, Lyle. 2024. Unclassified and Spurious Languages. Chapter 5 of: The Indigenous Languages of the Americas: History and Classification, pp. 280-338. New York: Oxford University Press. DOI 10.1093/oso/9780197673461.003.0005.
sources.note: Natterer's sixty words and short sentences discussed; unrelatable to known languages; no statement: nothing on stress, accent or tone anywhere in the chapter (the words stress/accent/tone/pitch/syllable do not occur); entry concerns attestation and classification only

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F.H. & Hélène B. Brijnen. 2014. Johann Natterer and the Amazonian languages. Revista Brasileira de Linguística Antropológica 6(2): 333-352. doi:10.26512/rbla.v6i2.16285.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.338 same sentence as above plus 'It has been suggested to belong to the Nambikwaran language family (Borella, pers. comm; Jolkesky, pers. comm).'; pp.339-340 on Natterer's diacritics (Bororo é = central vowel in one case, [e] in another; 'The motivation behind these different uses of é is not clear').

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F.H. & Hélène B. Brijnen. 2014. Natterer's Linguistic Heritage. Archiv Weltmuseum Wien 63-64 (Indigenous Heritage: Johann Natterer, Brazil, and Austria): 162-183. hdl.handle.net/1887/71532 (open access).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.166: 'The Cabixí language (from Mato Grosso), which may have been tonal judging from its structure and the diacritics added by Natterer, could not be assigned to any of the known existing language families.' p.176 lists the sample: W15 'Samples of the Cabixi Indians – from a boy who was taken to Mattogrosso when he was small – he was called Schirinimõ – his nation he calls Piacá. [1828–1829.]'; L12 'Cabischi in the forests and steppes along the Rio Galera in Matogrosso.' pp.167-168 discuss Natterer's diacritics in general (mostly uninterpretable today).

sources.note: Annotated edition of the Basel manuscript including the Cabixi (list 15) sample; the only place where the editors might expand on their 'may have been tonal.. diacritics' remark or interpret Natterer's accent marks. Would supersede the 2014 one-sentence conjecture, though a stress rule is not expected.
